chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who comes performing 'Umrah, intending the 'Umrah of Rajab, and the new moon enters before he reaches Al-'Aqiq. Should he enter the state of Ihram before the time [of Rajab] and designate it for Rajab, or should he delay the Ihram until Al-'Aqiq and designate it for Sha'ban? He said: 'He enters the state of Ihram before the time for Rajab, for Rajab has merit, and it is what he intended.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entering Ihram for 'Umrah if the new moon of Rajab appears before reaching the Miqat?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing the pilgrim's specific intention (Niyyah) and the spiritual merit of the month over rigid chronological alignment with the Miqat location. It underscores the flexibility in 'Umrah timing, allowing the act to be anchored to the lunar month of Rajab as soon as its arrival is confirmed, even if the physical entry into Ihram occurs slightly before the traditional boundary. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the sanctity of Rajab and the adaptability of ritual timing to ensure the worshiper captures the intended devotional state.
